components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--line-strong); border-radius: 6px; padding: 12px 20px; font-family: var(--font-bai-jamjuree), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.4; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 180ms ease, background-color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--text); background: var(--panel-soft); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-course-card { border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); font-family: var(--font-bai-jamjuree), system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-course-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-code { display: inline-block; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--text); color: var(--page); padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-course-card h3 { margin: 12px 0 0; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.55; font-weight: 600; } .ds-course-card p { margin: 4px 0 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.7; } .ds-credit { flex-shrink: 0; min-width: 56px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; text-align: center; } .ds-credit strong { display: block; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-credit span { color: var(--muted); font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-chip-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin-top: 16px; } .ds-chip-row span { border-radius: 6px; background: var(--panel-soft); color: var(--muted); padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; }

narrative.overview:
NextDST 69 should feel like a prepared study desk for a new DST student: ordered, quiet, and immediately useful. The interface serves lookup and orientation, so the visual system stays restrained, uses a single Thai-ready sans family, and keeps every surface close to the student's next action.

The product rejects difficult UX, hidden navigation, dense PDF-like pages, unclear filters, and decorative dashboard behavior. Visual decisions must help a student choose a year, read the study plan, scan course groups, and recover from empty results without guessing.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained neutral surfaces with one academic green accent.
Thai-first typography using Bai Jamjuree at practical product UI sizes.
Small-radius controls and cards that keep the interface compact.
Borders and tonal layering carry structure before shadows.
Motion is short and state-driven, never a page-load performance.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Use the green accent for current state, links, focus, and track information only. Do not add new hue families for course categories unless the data model requires it.

rules.name: The Neutral First Rule
rules.body: Structure the page with panel contrast, borders, spacing, and typography before reaching for saturated color.

rules.name: The Thai Readability Rule
rules.body: Do not compress Thai line-height to match English UI density. Thai body and helper text need enough vertical air to scan.

rules.name: The Product Scale Rule
rules.body: Avoid oversized marketing type. This is a curriculum tool, so headings should be stable, readable, and task-sized.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only for interactive lift or overlay hierarchy.

rules.name: The No Ghost Card Rule
rules.body: Do not pair a decorative wide shadow with a 1px border. If a card needs structure, use the existing border and low shadow vocabulary.

dos: Do use page, panel, panel-soft, and line to create structure before adding color.
Do keep the green accent rare and functional for focus, links, active states, and track chips.
Do preserve Bai Jamjuree as the only family unless the curriculum source demands a distinct monospace code treatment.
Do keep controls at least 44px tall on touch surfaces.
Do preserve visible focus states and reduced-motion alternatives for WCAG AA.
Do keep course data scannable through code badges, titles, credits, and metadata chips.
donts: Don't create difficult UX, hidden navigation, dense PDF-like pages, unclear filters, or interfaces that make students guess where to start.
Don't make the app feel like a generic marketing landing page or a decorative dashboard where visual style gets in the way of course lookup.
Don't use gradient text, glass cards, side-stripe card borders, or decorative chart-like hero metrics.
Don't add saturated category colors to every course group without a data reason.
Don't use motion that does not explain state changes. Product motion must stay between 150ms and 250ms unless the mobile drawer needs a stronger physical transition.
Don't hide the source document link or bury year navigation behind ambiguous labels.
